It’s a very specific crowd, very interconnected, you know? 

But for a while now, I’ve been entirely convinced that certain people in those exact circles are quietly tracking me. Specifically, they are keeping tabs on exactly which clients I meet with. And they aren't just doing it passively, they are sending me these little signals to let me know they're watching. It happens through these incredibly specific invitations I receive, or the panel topics that suddenly pop up at conferences right after I've had a private advisory meeting about that exact niche. It even comes down to who sits near me at networking events or charity dinners. The seating arrangements are completely deliberate, putting specific people next to me to send a message. 

And I sit there, and I try to be rational about it, I really do. I tell myself over and over that it could just be a coincidence, that Cincinnati is a small town in a lot of ways and these professional circles just naturally overlap. But no matter how much I try to logic my way out of it and brush it off, I can’t really let it go. I just can't. It just keeps happening, and it's taking up so much of my mental energy trying to decode what they are trying to say to me with all of this, because it's just too coordinated to be an accident...

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes a fixed belief that people in their professional circle are tracking them and sending them coordinated, deliberate signals through everyday events like seating arrangements and panel topics, which they cannot let go of despite trying to rationalize it as coincidence.

I mean, think about my day-to-day life. I get up at 5:30 AM every morning. I go for a run—well, a jog, really, usually just around the neighborhood, maybe three miles, nothing too intense but enough to get the blood flowing before the market opens. I make my coffee, I shower, I pick out my suit. I choose which tie matches which shirt. I drive my car to the office, taking the same route down I-71, dealing with the same morning traffic. I'm making hundreds of micro-decisions before I even sit down at my desk. If some outside force were controlling my body, wouldn't I feel like a puppet? Wouldn't I feel like my arm was moving to pour the coffee but I didn't tell it to? That sounds like something out of a science fiction movie, or maybe a really bad dream. 

And my actions at work, they have to be precise. I'm executing trades, rebalancing portfolios, making calls to clients to calm them down when the S&P dips. I have to be the one doing that. If someone else were controlling my hands on the keyboard, making trades I didn't authorize... I mean, the financial ruin that could cause is staggering. It would be a complete disaster. But that's not happening. I know exactly why I hit "buy" or "sell." I have the research reports right in front of me to back up every single keystroke. 

So no, I don't feel like a robot or a zombie or anything like that. I am completely autonomous. The issue, like I've been saying, isn't that someone is controlling me from the inside or making my body do things. It's the external environment. It's the people out there, in the arts community, the finance circles, the ones who are watching what I do and sending me those signals. They aren't controlling my actions; they are reacting to them. They are tracking my independent actions and using that information. But as for me, my body, my movements? 100% under my own jurisdiction. I've never felt otherwise, not even for a second.

Well, I guess... it’s not that I’m locking myself in a room or anything, but... yeah, things have definitely changed. I’m not socializing the way I used to. I used to be able to just dive into a massive portfolio review and crank it out, but lately, I just don't have the same spark. I’ll open up my client management software and see a whole list of follow-ups—you know, simple calls to touch base on a quarterly statement or check in on a trust account—and I just leave them sitting there. I’ll stare at the screen and think, I should really call Richard, but then I just... don't. I'll find some excuse to go get water or just stare out the window.

I’d go to these jazz nights downtown at this little place off 4th Street, or I'd play pickup basketball with some guys on Thursday nights. But lately, I just skip them. And the weirdest part is that I don't even really care that I'm missing out? Like, I skip the jazz nights or the basketball games without much feeling about it either way. It’s just a blank. The guys will text me saying they need a fifth for the court, and I just look at the text and put my phone face down. 

And then people notice, obviously. My friends or my brother will text me or call, asking what’s going on, why I’m not coming around or why I'm being so quiet, and I just... I don't know, I give them these really short answers. I'll just say, I'm good, or just tired, or work is busy. Just one or two words. Because honestly, just the idea of getting into it, of actually talking and carrying on a normal back-and-forth conversation... talking just feels like way more effort than it should. It’s like this massive physical drain just to form the sentences and project my voice and pretend to be engaged. It's exhausting. So I just give a short answer and stay home, because dealing with people just requires an energy level I can't seem to find right now.
